authBackendDecision: Supabase Auth remains the credential and session backend for now; Fieldgrid owns the application authentication boundary.

mandatoryDecisions.hostOnlyFieldgridAuthCookies: accepted; current host-only SameSite=Lax production-Secure behavior verified, HttpOnly not proven or configured
mandatoryDecisions.sessionRevocationRequirements: accepted target; current repository may not expose complete all-session provider revocation seam

jwtTenantClaimDependency: Do not depend on tenant_id JWT claims for personnel tenant binding; derive tenant identity from Fieldgrid host and database records.
resetModel: Challenge-code verification creates a short-lived reset grant; the grant authorizes password update and is invalidated after use, expiry, rate-limit lockout, profile disablement, tenant suspension, or session revocation.
currentCookieBehavior: Verified in artifacts/*/src/lib/supabase/session-cookies.ts: host-derived cookie name, no Domain attribute, path=/, SameSite=Lax, Secure only when NODE_ENV=production, no shared parent-domain cookie; HttpOnly is not currently proven or configured and @supabase/ssr browser/session behavior remains in use.
targetCookieRequirement: Move toward a server-only/HttpOnly session boundary where compatible; first prove refresh/login/logout behavior with browser E2E, document XSS and CSRF tradeoffs while cookies are browser-readable, and never claim HttpOnly until implemented and browser-tested.
currentRevocationCapability: Fieldgrid can require local cookie clearing and provider revocation calls through an adapter, but the current repository capability may not yet expose a complete all-session provider refresh-session revocation seam.
sessionRevocationRequirement: Password reset, admin reset, credential compromise, tenant suspension, profile inactivation, wrong-host detection, and support security action must revoke Fieldgrid cookies and provider refresh sessions as a mandatory target capability and acceptance requirement, not as a current full-implementation claim.
stepUpRequirement: Administrator and support reset operations require recent step-up/MFA before reset initiation, grant issuance, or session revocation changes.
